title_en: In Praise of the Holy Martyrs
author: Hesychius of Jerusalem
addressee: A congregation addressed as brothers and fathers
occasion: The surviving fragment is from encomia on martyrs, but the text itself does not state the occasion; the title indicates a festal address in praise of martyrs.
argument: The speaker calls the congregation to enter the Spirit's garden and gather not one virtue but all, since virtues depend on one another like stones in a tower or steps in a ladder. He then shows that each virtue is incomplete without another: fasting needs prayer, prayer needs almsgiving, almsgiving needs faith, gentleness needs humility, and faith needs love. Finally he urges the hearers to pursue all these virtues together, warning against being zealous in one area while negligent in another, because virtue brings joy even before the kingdom.

outline.move: The speaker invites the congregation into the Spirit's garden to gather all virtues, arguing that virtues require one another.
He shows that fasting is ineffective without prayer, and prayer cannot ascend without almsgiving.
He continues that almsgiving needs faith, gentleness needs humility, and faith without love is worthless.
He exhorts the hearers to pursue all the virtues together, not one at the expense of others, because virtue brings delight even before the kingdom.

cast.name: Cornelius
cast.who: A man named in the text whose prayers and alms were remembered before God; the fragment does not identify his role, though he is known from Acts as a centurion.

voices.speaker: Jesus
voices.how_marked: Introduced by φησίν (he says) and quoted directly

voices.speaker: The angel
voices.how_marked: Introduced as the angel speaking to Cornelius

voices.speaker: Unnamed scriptural speaker
voices.how_marked: Introduced only by φησίν (he says) without a named speaker

key_terms.sense: Virtue or excellence of character, the central theme of the homily
Almsgiving or deeds of mercy toward the poor
The crown or wreath of martyrdom and victory
The kingdom of heaven, the final reward

scripture: The author quotes the Gospels and Pauline epistles in forms close to the Greek New Testament; Psalms are not cited in this fragment. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and numbering.
uncertain: The exact date of the homily is unknown.
The attribution to Hesychius of Jerusalem is marked as doubtful in the source.
The original occasion or feast day for the homily is not stated in the surviving fragment.
The speaker of the saying in u01-rem-early ("This kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting") is not named in the text.
The speaker of the saying in u01-rem-mid ("If I have faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing") is not named in the text.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Unnamed scriptural speaker introduced only by φησίν (he says) without a named speaker in sections ["u01-rem-early", "u01-rem-mid"]
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: «Τοῦτο γάρ», φησίν, «τὸ γένος οὐκ ἐξέρχεται εἰ μὴ ἐν νηστείᾳ καὶ προσευχῇ.»
_unresolved_facts.fix: The saying "This kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting" is spoken by Jesus (Mark 9:29/Matthew 17:21). The brief should identify this as Jesus, not as an unnamed scriptural speaker. The brief's own uncertain list correctly notes this is unmarked, but the voices entry misclassifies it.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jesus introduced by φησίν (he says) and quoted directly in sections ["u01-rem-mid"]
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: «Μάθετε γὰρ ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, φησίν, ὅτι πραΰς εἰμι καὶ ταπεινὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ.»
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jesus is introduced by φησίν in u01-rem-mid, but the brief should note that two other sayings in u01-rem-mid ("Eleemosynais and pistis..." and "If I have faith...") are also introduced by φησίν without named speakers. The brief's uncertain list correctly identifies the latter as unnamed, but the voices entry only captures one of three φησίν instances in u01-rem-mid.

_unresolved_facts.claim: fasting needs prayer, prayer needs almsgiving, almsgiving needs faith, gentleness needs humility, and faith needs love
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Θαυμαστὴ μὲν οὖν ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη, ἀλλὰ χωρὶς πίστεως ἁμαρτημάτων οὐκ ἐργάζεται λύτρωσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text says almsgiving without faith does not accomplish "ransom/release of sins" (ἁμαρτημάτων...λύτρωσιν), not that almsgiving "needs faith" in the same structural pattern. The brief oversimplifies: the text says almsgiving without faith doesn't work for redemption of sins, using a scriptural quotation about almsgiving and faith together cleansing sins.

_unresolved_facts.claim: virtue brings joy even before the kingdom
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὕτως ἡ ἀρετὴ τοὺς ἐργαζομένους αὐτὴν καὶ πρὸ τῆς βασιλείας παρασκευάζει τρυφᾶν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The text says virtue "prepares those who practice it to feast/delight even before the kingdom" (παρασκευάζει τρυφᾶν), not that virtue itself brings joy. The brief's "virtue brings joy" is imprecise; the Greek emphasizes preparation (παρασκευάζει) for feasting/delight (τρυφᾶν), and the contrast is with vice punishing even before Gehenna.
